miss master[1]: actor has the target drop the chin while defender and room describe slipping the angle with masterful timing; compatible, left as is.
weak expert[2]: defender line describes a light clamp at the windpipe rather than the feint high, drive low the actor and room see; compatible but loose.
wait beginner[2]: actor keeps pressure with the weapon poised while defender and room only see the attacker watch the throat; compatible wait text.
prepare master[1]: actor gains angles from the target's movement, defender sees head shifts read, room sees posture read; same beat, three phrasings.
critical beginner[2] and expert[2]: banner forms DEVASTATE/DEVASTATED/DEVASTATES and ANNIHILATE/ANNIHILATION differ only by inflection; the guard accepts them.
Many actor lines (weak expert[1], weak master[0], heavy expert[0], heavy master[3] and others) never name {actee}; not a room line rule, noted only.
cleaving: weak master: the swaps and observer rewrites form one set; apply them together. Slot roles touched by a swap are never also rewritten, so every 'old' is the line in the file now.
prepare beginner[3] actor 'You stance yourself aggressively' uses stance as a verb; the defender's 'shoulders' sits loosely beside 'raised'.
wait beginner[0] room line 'stalks around' while the actor only watches; compatible but loose.
wait expert[0] room line 'eyes warily' while actor and defender circle; compatible but loose.
wait expert[3] defender line 'holds their item steady' while actor and room probe the guard; compatible but loose.
miss expert[1] room line names the defender but not the attacker ('the feint').
miss master[1] actor line runs past 80 visible characters.
normal master[7] after the swap the defender line is the plain 'chops into your {bodypart}' against the actor's solid cleave; same blow, plainer copy.
normal master[9] defender line says 'cleaves ... brutal swing' where actor and room say 'chops ... precise swing'.

prepare master 3: defender line only says the attacker prepares with flowing grace and names no stance.
